question_text: Write the complex number (2 − 3i)(3 + 4i) in the form A + iB.

mark_split.label: Use i² = −1 and write A + iB

recall_prompt: Say how you would write this product in the form A + iB.
insider_note: The second mark is one substitution, i² = −1: it turns −12i² into +12 and makes the real part 6 + 12 = 18. And B is the real number −1, not −i — the form A + iB has both A and B real.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply out
steps.margin_note: First mark. Four products, like any two binomials: 2·3, 2·4i, −3i·3, −3i·4i.
steps.memory_tip: Four products, like any two binomials: 2·3, 2·4i, −3i·3, −3i·4i.

recall.must_convey: That the brackets are multiplied term by term to give 6 + 8i − 9i − 12i².
accept: multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second to get six plus eight i minus nine i minus twelve i squared

steps.why: Complex numbers multiply exactly like binomials in i. The only new thing happens in the next line, when i² is replaced.

steps.label: Use i² = −1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. −12i² = +12, so the real part is 6 + 12 = 18. The i terms combine to −i.
steps.memory_tip: −12i² = +12, so A = 18. B is the real number −1, never −i.

recall.must_convey: That i² = −1 turns −12i² into +12, giving 18 − i, so A = 18 and B = −1.

steps.why: The form A + iB means one real number and one real coefficient of i. Naming A and B at the end is what the question literally asks for.
